title: Different ends can share a state
hook: Different ends can share a state. Follow the computed steps.

knows: Compare numbers; read a short array, string, tree or graph as drawn.
doesNotKnow: Group substrings by end-position equivalence and split states when a new extension changes that equivalence.

misconception: Every distinct substring needs its own automaton state.
objective: Group substrings by end-position equivalence and split states when a new extension changes that equivalence.

claims.text: A clone splits a state when a transition would mix different substring length intervals. Suffix links then give each state its exact interval of lengths sharing the same continuation behaviour.
